correctness.rationale: Every subset has zero, one or at least two occupied backbone branches. With one branch the star classification yields \(A_i+z+a_i z^2\). With extremes \(i<j\) selected spine centers are allowed only alone at the extremes, and the internal branches allow only selected leaves, yielding \(E_iE_j\prod A_k\). Unique shortest paths show necessity and sufficiency. Disjoint decomposition proves the generating polynomial; straightforward inductive coefficient recurrence follows. Boundaries \(r=1\) and \(a_i=0\) are valid. Independent BFS triple testing verified 992 profiles, covering 2,806,538 vertex subsets, plus 111 known-family cases; these finite tests do not prove the unrestricted identity.

value.rationale: The 2024 polynomial program explicitly counts brooms and uniform combs but lacks heterogeneous caterpillar counts. A complete all-set classification and \(O(N^2)\) coefficient recurrence for arbitrary pendant profiles is a natural and useful extension, not a scalar parameter substitution. It preserves exact cardinality distributions across many branching positions, and exposes nonisomorphic seven-vertex caterpillars with identical degree multisets but different polynomials. No assertion of downstream universal theorem or unimodality is needed.
